title: "The Bus Door Kept Flying Open at High Speed": A Passenger's Nsukka to Lagos Nightmare
excerpt: A real story shared inside our travellers' group: what happened when an Okeyson Hiace bus from Nsukka to Cele, Lagos hit the expressway with a faulty sliding door—and how to protect yourself before boarding.
content:
When you pay for an interstate ticket, you expect basic safety—working brakes, good tyres, and a door that actually stays shut on the highway. Unfortunately, one member of our travellers' community learned the hard way that checking a bus before it leaves the park can save your life.

Here is their unfiltered account of a recent trip from Nsukka to Cele, Lagos on an Okeyson Hiace bus.

"Every Pothole Made My Heart Skip"

"Omo, this was one of the worst travelling experiences I have ever had. I boarded an Okeyson Hiace bus from Nsukka heading to Cele, Lagos, thinking I was simply going to have a normal journey. Little did I know that the trip would turn into a terrifying experience that I would never forget. From the moment we started moving, I noticed something was wrong with the door, but I never imagined how dangerous it would become.

The door was not properly working. Anytime the driver hit a pothole, bump, or the vehicle galloped, the door would suddenly open by itself. Imagine sitting inside a bus moving at high speed on the highway, with a faulty door right beside you. Every time the bus jumped on a bad portion of the road and that door popped open, my heart would literally skip. I kept wondering what would happen if it swung open completely while the bus was speeding.

What made the whole situation worse was that I was sitting right next to that door. While other passengers were trying to relax and sleep during the journey, I couldn’t even close my eyes. I had to stay fully awake and constantly watch the latch. Every pothole, every sudden brake, and every gallop made me nervous. At some point, I started imagining the worst-case scenario—someone being thrown out of the bus while the vehicle was still moving. It was no longer just an uncomfortable journey; I genuinely felt unsafe.

Instead of getting some rest on the long road from Nsukka to Lagos, I spent the entire trip fighting sleep and holding onto my nerves. My body was exhausted, but fear kept me awake. Each time the door suddenly opened, I would jolt awake and wonder why the driver kept pushing on without properly fixing it.

By the time we finally arrived at Cele, Lagos, I was completely drained—not just from the distance, but from hours of non-stop tension. Honestly, a commercial bus carrying human beings should never be put on the expressway with a door in that condition. I sincerely hope Okeyson takes this complaint seriously so no other passenger goes through what I experienced."

3 Things to Check Before Your Bus Leaves the Park

Stories like this happen every week on Nigerian highways—especially during busy travel periods when operators rush vehicles back onto the road without proper maintenance. Before you drop your bag in the boot, take 10 seconds to check:

  • Test the sliding door lock yourself: If you are seated in the row beside the door, pull the handle firmly from the inside before the bus hits the highway. If the latch feels loose or requires rope/wire to stay shut, demand another seat or switch buses immediately.
  • Inspect the tyres and dashboard warning lights: Bald front tyres on routes like Benin–Ore or Lokoja–Abuja are a major hazard during sudden braking.
  • Ask fellow travellers first: Park loaders will tell you every bus is "brand new with full AC." Only recent passengers will tell you which operator is actually maintaining their fleet this month.
